sources.entry: OpenHabitTracker - Track habits, tasks and notes with time tracking, calendar view and completion statistics. (Demo, Source Code) GPL-3.0 Docker
OpenHabitTracker - Take notes, plan tasks, track habits. Free, open source, all data stays on your device.

summary.one_liner: OpenHabitTracker is a free, open-source app for taking notes, planning tasks and tracking habits, with data kept on your device and optional sync to a server you host yourself.
summary.what_it_does: The app combines Markdown notes, tasks with planned dates, durations, checklists and timers, and habits scored by how overdue they are rather than by streaks. Lists can be searched, filtered by date, category, priority and status, and sorted with eleven keys. Weekly statistics and per-habit charts show progress, history, calendar views, longest streaks and weekday patterns. Daily notifications summarize due tasks and overdue habits, and data can be imported and exported as JSON, YAML, TSV, Markdown or a Google Keep Takeout ZIP. The README also describes a Docker image that runs a Blazor Server app for a single user, which the desktop and mobile clients can sync with.
use_cases: track daily habits without streak pressure
keep Markdown notes alongside to-do lists
self-host a single-user habit and task tracker
sync a personal planner between devices via my own server
import Google Keep notes into a task app
how_to_run: Create a .env file with APPSETTINGS_USERNAME, APPSETTINGS_EMAIL, APPSETTINGS_PASSWORD and APPSETTINGS_JWT_SECRET
Generate the JWT secret with: openssl rand -base64 32 (Linux/macOS) or the PowerShell RandomNumberGenerator command in the README (Windows)
Save the README's docker-compose.yml next to .env and set TZ to your timezone
Open the server on port 5050 (or the port you mapped) to confirm it runs
In the app, go to Menu > Data > Online sync, enter the server address, username and password, then click Log in
notable: Habit progress measured as percent overdue (e.g. a 10-day habit 2 days overdue reads 120%) instead of streaks
Runs on Windows, Linux, Android, iOS, macOS, as a web app, and self-hosted
Data stays on device; sync goes only to a server you run yourself
Filters for planned and done dates work relative to today, so saved filters stay current
Localized into about twenty languages and offers 26 themes
caveats: The Docker server is described as a single-user app
Sync requires you to host and configure the Docker container yourself
Store links in the README are empty, so the availability of each platform build is not confirmed beyond the list of platforms
